item.title: U.S. military reveals it has deployed weapons in space
item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with space security analyst Laura Grego of the Union of Concerned Scientists about the U.S. military's revelation that it has deployed weapons in space.
item.content:encoded: NPR's A Martinez speaks with space security analyst Laura Grego of the Union of Concerned Scientists about the U.S. military's revelation that it has deployed weapons in space.
item.dc:creator: A Martínez

item.title: U.S. acknowledges for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space
item.description: The remarkable revelation comes after previous warnings about countries such as Russia possibly weaponizing a global frontier long agreed in treaties to be used for only peaceful purposes.
item.content:encoded:
The remarkable revelation comes after previous warnings about countries such as Russia possibly weaponizing a global frontier long agreed in treaties to be used for only peaceful purposes.

(Image credit: Matt Rourke/)

item.title: NASA rushed engineers out of their labs. They say it risks future space missions
item.description: NASA employees say they've lost vital equipment and staff needed to make sophisticated spacecraft amid the agency's abrupt relocations over the past several months.
item.content:encoded:
NASA employees say they've lost vital equipment and staff needed to make sophisticated spacecraft amid the agency's abrupt relocations over the past several months.

(Image credit: Jolearra Tshiteya)

item.title: NASA relocations could hinder agency's ability to build spacecraft
item.description: NASA has been moving engineers out of their labs as a way to reduce waste. But the moves may be limiting the agency's ability to make spacecraft.
item.content:encoded: NASA has been moving engineers out of their labs as a way to reduce waste. But the moves may be limiting the agency's ability to make spacecraft.

item.title: New telescope will help scientists study a mysterious force called 'dark energy'
item.description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks science reporter Joe Palca about the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which will have a field of view at least 100 times larger than Hubble Space Telescope.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks science reporter Joe Palca about the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which will have a field of view at least 100 times larger than Hubble Space Telescope.
item.dc:creator: Joe Palca

item.title: 'A glorious dawn launch': NASA's newest space telescope has left the Earth
item.description: The tour-bus-sized telescope aims to unravel cosmic mysteries and identify more than 100,000 planets beyond our solar system.
item.content:encoded:
The tour-bus-sized telescope aims to unravel cosmic mysteries and identify more than 100,000 planets beyond our solar system.

item.title: NASA is about to launch a space telescope that could change how we see the universe
item.description: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches Aug. 30 on a mission to explore some of the most pressing mysteries of the cosmos.
item.content:encoded:
NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches Aug. 30 on a mission to explore some of the most pressing mysteries of the cosmos.

(Image credit: NASA)
item.dc:creator: Joe Palca

item.title: NASA's latest telescope will explore dark energy and other cosmic mysteries
item.description: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, set to launch this weekend, may shed new light on the nature of dark energy -- that mysterious force causing the universe to expand.
item.content:encoded: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, set to launch this weekend, may shed new light on the nature of dark energy -- that mysterious force causing the universe to expand.

item.title: A NASA telescope is slowly plummeting to earth and there's no way to save it
item.description: NASA's Swift Observatory has orbited the Earth since 2004. It's now falling towards earth, and after a failed mission to save it, NASA is leaving the doomed telescope to its fate.
item.content:encoded: NASA's Swift Observatory has orbited the Earth since 2004. It's now falling towards earth, and after a failed mission to save it, NASA is leaving the doomed telescope to its fate.

item.title: This high-speed star is whipping around the black hole in the middle of our galaxy
item.description: Researchers have identified a speed demon at the heart of the Milky Way. This fast-moving star may yield insights into the black hole parked at the center of our galaxy.
